evidence.V1: Front outline is a clean symmetric octagonal crown over a pointed pavilion (A15 X/Y error 0.0); the silhouette and top view read instantly as a cut gem at 64 px from front, three-quarter and top.
evidence.V2: Clear hierarchy: big crown-vs-pavilion split at the girdle, medium octagonal table plus 8 crown and 8 pavilion facets, small chamfer strips along every facet edge.
evidence.V3: Confident stylised gem: shallow chunky crown, wide table, pavilion short enough to stay toy-like; no stiff-primitive look.
evidence.V4: Uniform narrow chamfers on table ring, crown facet joins and girdle catch light consistently in the studio close-ups and the top view.
evidence.V5: Crown and pavilion close-ups (studio + flat) show flat, crisp facets with no pinches, seams or z-fighting; faceting is by design and the culet tip closes cleanly.
evidence.V6: Single hue in three values (light table, mid crown, dark pavilion) with strong value contrast; colourways (crimson, shadow) keep the same disciplined 3-value structure.
evidence.V7: 286 tris against a small-class target of 600 (ceiling 1500), budget_note ok.
evidence.V8: One white LF_VertexColor material with vertex colours, ~kit-scale chamfers and smooth shading; looks indistinguishable from the kit gem reference.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct for a pickup: CanCollide off, CanTouch on, CollisionFidelity Box, Anchored, MeshPart.Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin centre.

top_fixes: Optional: add a slightly lighter value on the pavilion facet nearest the light so the underside reads less near-black in dark scenes
Optional: a touch more crown height would strengthen the side silhouette at very small sizes
